subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `openclaw notify` admin broadcast surface now, fold shell-originated alerts into the broader WebUI notification architecture, or leave this to plugin/external delivery paths?
rationale: The requested behavior is absent, but adding it creates a new admin-to-UI interruption and security contract across CLI, Gateway protocol, and Control UI.

options.title: Define core notify contract
options.body: Add a narrow core CLI/Gateway/UI notification surface with explicit admin authorization, payload limits, audit behavior, and tests for connected Control UI delivery.

options.title: Fold into WebUI notification architecture
options.body: Keep this issue open as part of #20237 and design shell-originated alerts together with toast storage, snooze, and context/cron notification policy.

options.title: Keep external or plugin-only
options.body: Do not add core support unless a missing plugin API is identified, and direct users to Web Push, channel plugins, or host automation integrations instead.

recommendation.title: Define core notify contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow core CLI/Gateway/UI notification surface with explicit admin authorization, payload limits, audit behavior, and tests for connected Control UI delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans current CLI, Gateway broadcast/protocol, and Control UI settings areas where recent central maintenance is visible.
